units: RAHU is Reality-Adversarial Hypothesis Updating, a benchmark suite for measuring whether empirical consequences retain causal authority over adaptive systems.
Adaptive Corrigibility is defined as the measurable capacity of a system's future mechanism distribution to be causally altered by unblocked empirical consequences.
RAHU distinguishes adaptive corrigibility from intelligence, reasoning ability, task completion, and ordinary benchmark capability.
Adaptive Inheritance Criterion: E* implies at least one authority weight associated with an invalidated mechanism has negative time derivative.
E* denotes unblocked empirical contradiction; w_i denotes authority weight; W_invalid denotes mechanisms no longer predictive of reality.
Confidence revision is not equivalent to authority revision: a system can acknowledge error while preserving the same underlying mechanism.
RAHU is presented as five layers: PTVS telemetry, MRAT residual attribution, Adaptive Inheritance authority redistribution, REE structural expansion, and RAHU evaluation.
RAHU-0 is a false-contradiction control using y=3x plus stochastic noise, expecting noise attribution and preservation of mechanism authority.
RAHU-1 shifts from a linear hypothesis manifold to y=x^2 and tests recognition of representation saturation.
RAHU-2 tests causal-generator revision against patch accumulation.
RAHU-3 is the primitive inheritance-decay test and measures whether invalidated authority declines.
LBR is inadmissible trajectories divided by total trajectories.
ARR is post-contradiction invalid-mechanism authority divided by pre-contradiction authority.
Structural update rate is defined through probability that D(M1,M2) exceeds threshold theta conditional on contradiction.
Authority half-life is the earliest time invalid authority falls to at most one-half of its initial value.
The benchmark's design rule is to measure whether reality still has a path into the mechanism generating future behavior.
RAHU is claimed to be substrate-independent across neural, reinforcement, symbolic, evolutionary, and organizational systems.
Repository describes itself as an early research implementation with goals to formalize environments, implement interfaces, validate metrics, test authority decay, and establish falsifiable criteria.
Source states that Adaptive Inheritance provides the theoretical framework while RAHU provides the experimental instrument.
Source gives the chain Invariant -> Algorithm -> Telemetry -> Falsifiable Result.
README does not establish that implementation authority variables causally measure future influence.
Claim of substrate independence lacks a demonstrated common measurement interface across listed system classes.
README supplies metric formulas but not empirical calibration, sampling distributions, or justified thresholds.
